decision.reason: Legal answer in paragraph 1 is the strength; half the article is for couples who qualify; the Australian route is hidden under the religious heading.

findings.issue: 'Ask your mairie' in most table cells; 'sworn translator' unexplained; never says the Australian route avoids nearly all French paperwork.
Route 2 (legal in Australia, celebration in France) has no heading; buried under 'Religious and symbolic ceremonies'.
Church-after-Australian-wedding left open; New Caledonia option raised and dropped; no cost picture.
No France track record; 'partnered planner' raises the commission worry (CONCIERGE-PAY).
Hard sentences and undefined terms (parent's house line, NOIM, CNI, sworn translator, overseas collectivity).
Cost FAQ dodges; no comparison with Italy (Italy allows non-residents to marry legally, per our Italy guide).

payload.in_their_words: Good, someone finally says it straight... the bit that's actually for us is hidden under the church heading... Saving it for Marcus, but I'm not booking a call yet.
